# `js/import-no-named-as-default`

**A default import must not take the name of a named export**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/project` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the binding needs a name of the author's choosing for the default export; the code holds only the named export's) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-import/no-named-as-default`, `eslint-plugin-import-x/no-named-as-default` |

## What it checks

`import x from "./m"` where `./m` has a default export and also exports `x` by name is reported at the default specifier: it is usually the named export that was meant (`import { x }`). Where the two exports are one binding — `export { x }` beside `export default x`, or two re-exports of the same name from the same module — nothing is reported; upstream cannot tell a local binding exported twice from two, and reports it. A module with no default export is the `js/import-default` rule's.

**Why:** `import helper from` reads like the named `helper` and is the module's default, which is a different value; the code runs and does the wrong thing.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/project` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/project"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/import-no-named-as-default" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/import-no-named-as-default" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/import-no-named-as-default" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/import-no-named-as-default" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/import-no-named-as-default" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/import-no-named-as-default": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/import-no-named-as-default: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/import-no-named-as-default expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/import-no-named-as-default --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/import-no-named-as-default       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/import-no-named-as-default  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                 # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. If the named export was meant, import it: `import { helper } from "./lib"`.
2. If the default was meant, give the binding a name that is not one of the module's named exports.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
// src/lib.js
export const helper = () => 1;
export default function main() {}
// src/app.js
import helper from "./lib";
console.log(helper());
```

#### Do

```js files
// src/lib.js
export const helper = () => 1;
export default function main() {}
// src/app.js
import main, { helper } from "./lib";
console.log(main, helper());
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
// src/lib.jsx
export const helper = () => 1;
export default function main() {}
// src/app.jsx
import helper from "./lib";
console.log(helper());
```

#### Do

```jsx files
// src/lib.jsx
export const helper = () => 1;
export default function main() {}
// src/app.jsx
import main, { helper } from "./lib";
console.log(main, helper());
```

#### Do
